chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habeeb al-Sajistani, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who cut the two right hands of two men. He said: 'O Habeeb! His right hand is cut for the man whose right hand he cut first, and his left hand is cut for the man whose right hand he cut last, because he only cut the hand of the last man, and his right hand is retaliation for the first man.'

He said: 'I said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to cut the right hand and the left leg.' He said: 'Indeed, he used to do that regarding what is obligatory from the Rights of Allah. But as for the Rights of the Muslims, O Habeeb, their rights are taken for them in retaliation: the hand for the hand, if the cutter has a hand, and the leg for the hand, if the cutter does not have a hand.'

So I said to him: 'Does it not obligate the wergild upon him, and his leg is left for him?' He said: 'The wergild is only obligated upon him when he cuts a man's hand, and the cutter has neither two hands nor two legs; then the wergild is obligated upon him because he has no limb from which retaliation can be taken.'

key_terms.جَارِحَةٌ: Limb or organ used for retaliation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for qisas when a person cuts two right hands of two different men?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of qisas for limb amputation, distinguishing between personal rights (huquq al-ibad) and divine rights (huquq Allah). It establishes that for personal injuries, the perpetrator's right hand is taken for the first victim and the left for the second, contrasting with the Prophet's practice of cutting the right hand and left foot for divine rights cases. Furthermore, it clarifies that wergild (diyah) is only due if the perpetrator lacks sufficient limbs for direct retaliation, ensuring precise retribution.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Habeeb Al Sajistany who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a man who cut two right hands of two men. O Habeeb! His right hand would be cut for the first man whose right hand he had cut, and his left would be cut for the last man whose right hand he had cut, because he cut the hand of the last one, and his own right hand had already been cut in retaliation for the first man’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘But rather, Ali<sup>asws</sup> used to cut the right hand and the left leg?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, he<sup>asws</sup> used to do that with regards to what was Obligated from the Rights of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. O Habeeb! So, as for the rights of the Muslims, he<sup>asws</sup> used to take their rights for them with regards to the retaliation, the hand for the hand, if it was such that the cutter had a hand and a leg, and the leg for the hand when there did not happen to be a hand for the cutter’.

So I said to him, ‘Or does it not Obligate the wergild upon him, and his leg is left for him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, it Obligated the wergild upon him when a hand of a man is cut, and there are no two hands or two legs for the cutter, so then the wergild would be Obligated upon him, because there is no limb for him to be retaliated from’.
